requirements.text: The FSW shall process science data from the camera and relay it to the Spacecraft Control Unit (SCU) in the form of CCSDS Source Packets.
The FSW shall receive commands from the SCU that establish the current instrument state and camera mode.
The FSW shall transmit detailed housekeeping data to the SCU in the form of CCSDS Source Packets.
The FSW shall receive a time message from the SCU and synchronize the XCP local copy of the spacecraft clock.
The FSW shall control the heaters on the telescope tube and on the thermal baffles.
The FSW shall read the TAM.
The FSW shall validate the integrity of all received telecommands using a checksum or CRC and verify that the command source is authorized before execution.
The FSW shall ensure the integrity of transmitted telemetry packets using cryptographic signatures or message authentication codes (MACs) to prevent tampering.
The FSW shall process and buffer science data at a sustained rate of at least 100kbps and handle burst inputs of up to 60,000 pixels/sec without data loss.
The FSW shall maintain heater temperatures within the range of [TBD] to [TBD] degrees Celsius and enter a safe state if sensor readings are out of range or indicate a hardware failure.
The FSW shall synchronize the local clock to the spacecraft time with an accuracy of better than [TBD] milliseconds.
The FSW shall process and buffer science data at a sustained rate of at least 120 kbps and support a burst throughput of 500 kbps without data loss.
The FSW shall execute heater control loops at a frequency of at least 1 Hz with a temperature regulation accuracy of +/- 0.5 degrees Celsius.
The FSW shall synchronize the local clock to the spacecraft time with an accuracy of better than 1 millisecond.
The FSW shall sample the TAM data and perform centroid calculations at a minimum rate of 10 Hz with a processing latency of less than 50 milliseconds.

OPEN: The PRD does not define the security posture or access control requirements for the Engineering Ethernet interface, which is present on Engineering Units. - The FSW shall implement restricted access controls for the Engineering Ethernet interface, ensuring that only authenticated ground support equipment can access diagnostic or configuration functions.

OPEN: The PRD does not define the recovery behavior for the 'XRT Centroid Error' or other critical failure states beyond simple message transmission. - Upon detection of a persistent centroid error or hardware fault, the FSW shall transition to a safe state and attempt a controlled reset or notify the SCU for intervention.
